newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says to reach budget goal agreed with IMF.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says to reach budget goal agreed with IMF.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday its general government deficit will be below four percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) this year as agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The IMF granted a $387 million stand-by loan to Hungary in March. One of the IMF's key conditions was that the country should keep the central budget deficit below four percent of the GDP.

Finance Ministry Deputy Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told a news conference that certain general government expenditures will be larger than previously expected but the budget will be compensated from surplus revenues.
He said the deficit of the social security is likely to run up to 50 to 60 billion forints this year, which would be some three times larger than the original 17.8 billion forint target.
Hungary may also spend 10 to 15 billion forints more for housing finance state subsidies this year than targeted, he added.

However, the central budget will generate more than planned revenues from customs duties, corporate taxes and foreign assets, and this will help Hungary to reach the budget target agreed with the IMF, Laszlo said.
"But we have to put more emphasis on the structural reforms," he added, referring to the social security's soaring deficit.
